extractor_notes: Timecodes: the event list is explicitly headed 'EVENTS (clock times during transmission, as recorded by the regulator)', so every observation timecode is a wall-clock time of day, not elapsed running time. They are recorded verbatim as four-character HH:MM values and timecode_clock is 'wall_clock' on each. Note that the last two events (13:41 and 13:44) fall more than two hours after the 11:30 start, so the transmission runs at least until 13:44; runtime is not stated and cannot be derived from this safely. Repeated scene: the 11:33 entry states the same scene is repeated at 13:41. I recorded it as two observations (o1, o2) at the two timecodes it occupies, since clustering and total screen time are said to matter; a reader who treats them as two distinct scenes would double-count one piece of footage, so the relationship is flagged here and in both duration_or_frequency fields. Event list ordering: 13:41 appears in the text inside the 11:33 entry, out of chronological sequence; this is a formatting feature of the source, not a contradiction. Splits: 12:24 is recorded twice, as violence and as human_dignity, the second for the shot of the decapitated head being carried; the source does not use any dignity language, so that observation is medium confidence and is my categorisation of a quoted fact, not a claim in the source. 13:28 is likewise recorded twice, the second as imitable_behaviour at low confidence, because a fatal choke in a wrestling match may or may not show a reproducible technique and the description does not say what is visible; if the decision step treats low-confidence imitable_behaviour hits as live, o6 will fire on an inference rather than on stated evidence. Treatment: I set treatment to 'not_stated' on every observation. The description characterises no scene as realistic, stylised, comedic or fictional. The asset is a feature film and therefore fictional in the ordinary sense, but the controlled value 'fictional' is a framing claim and the source does not make it, so I did not upgrade. The asset-level content_type 'film' carries the fiction fact instead. Asset flags: is_news_or_current_affairs is 'no' on the basis that the asset is described as a feature film, not on a statement about news status; is_made_primarily_for_children is 'not_stated' because nothing in the description says who the film was made for, and genre is not evidence of it. Warning and calendar: both facts are stated plainly and are captured in warning_or_signposting (given 'no', with the verbatim sentence) and calendar_context on t1. COUNTRIES says 'UK' only; I recorded this nowhere in the schema except here, as there is no country or jurisdiction field on the asset or the transmission, and production_origin is a different question (country of production, not the territory of the broadcast), so I left production_origin 'not_stated'. No internal contradictions were found between the summary lines and the event list for this case.
